common_name: Apple Crisp Heuchera (Crisped Green and White-Veiled Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Apple Crisp is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction. The tightly crisped leaf texture distinguishes it from smoother-leaved green heucheras.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Apple Crisp is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with seriously crisped, ruffled green leaves overlaid with a white veil. Short white flowers rise above the foliage mound. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Berry Marmalade Heuchera (Large Silver-Veiled Black-Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Berry Marmalade is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction. Part of the Heuchera MARMALADE series bred for extra-thick leaves and tolerance of both intense heat and cold.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Berry Marmalade is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with deep purple-black leaves overlaid with a silvery veil on an extra-large, thick-leaved plant. White flowers bloom on 18-inch stems in June and July. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Black Forest Cake Heuchera (Smooth Chocolate Foliage with Cherry-Red Flowers)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Black Forest Cake is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Black Forest Cake is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with smooth, dark chocolatey foliage. Bright cherry-red flowers contrast against the dark leaves. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Champagne Heuchera (Peach-to-Champagne-Gold Coral Bells with Maroon Flower Stems)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Champagne is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction. The seasonal color shift toward champagne-gold gives the cultivar its name.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Champagne is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with medium-size leaves that shift from peach to gold to champagne-gold under a strong white veil. Free-flowering maroon stems carry light peach flowers for most of the season. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Cherry Cola Heuchera (Rust-Red Coral Bells with Cherry-Red Flowers)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Cherry Cola is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction. Part of the Heuchera SODA series.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Cherry Cola is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with rust-red leaves that appear more vivid in sun and more veiled in shade. Cherry-red flowers bloom on 18-inch stems in April through June. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Creme Brule Heuchera (Peachy-Orange to Amber Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Creme Brule is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction, distinct from the Proven Winners Dolce series cultivar 'Creme Brulee' already in the trade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Creme Brule is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with peachy-orange spring leaves maturing to amber in summer. White and yellow flowers rise on stems to about 22 inches. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Georgia Plum Heuchera (Compact Rose-Purple Sport of Georgia Peach)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Georgia Plum is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction, a mutation out of 'Georgia Peach' with a tighter habit, smaller leaves, and shorter flower stems than its parent.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Georgia Plum is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with year-round rose-purple leaves with a pink-to-silver overlay. Purple-pink flowers appear on shorter stems than its parent cultivar. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Lemon Supreme Heuchera (Clean Yellow Rounded-Mound Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Lemon Supreme is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction, part of its yellow-leaved coral bells lineup.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Lemon Supreme is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with clean yellow, round leaves emerging yellow in spring and turning lime in summer, forming a rounded mound. White flowers rise above the chartreuse-yellow mound. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Lime Ruffles Heuchera (Large Ruffled Lime-Green Villosa Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Lime Ruffles is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction bred using Heuchera villosa parentage, giving it larger leaves and better heat tolerance than many ruffled cultivars.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Lime Ruffles is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with very large, ruffled lime-green leaves with a frosty white overlay. Attractive white flowers appear in fall on medium spikes. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Paprika Heuchera (Cherry-Coral Foliage with Seasonal Color Shift)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Paprika is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction named for its spicy, warm coral-orange seasonal foliage color shift.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Paprika is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with large, warm, glowing cherry-coral foliage that shifts from bright rose-orange in early spring to orange in summer with a white veil, to burgundy with a white veil in fall. White flowers bloom on 12-inch spikes in May and June. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Paris White Heuchera (Green-Leaved Coral Bells with Long-Blooming Ivory Flowers)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Paris White is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction, a white-flowered companion selection related to the earlier introduction 'Paris', grown primarily for its exceptionally long ivory-white bloom season rather than foliage color.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Paris White is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with green foliage forming a tidy mound. Elegant ivory-white flowers bloom in great numbers and keep flowering right up until frost. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Peach Crisp Heuchera (Extremely Ruffled Peach-to-Amber Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Peach Crisp is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction. The heavily crisped, ruffled leaf margin is the namesake trait of this cultivar.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Peach Crisp is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells introduction with extremely ruffled leaves in peach-to-amber shades. White flowers bloom on 15-inch stems in May and June. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Mojito Heucherella (Gold-to-Lime Foliage with Red Veins, Few Flower Spikes)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Mojito is a Terra Nova Nurseries heucherella introduction bred for a low-flowering habit that keeps the gold-to-lime foliage display uninterrupted through the season.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Mojito is a Terra Nova Nurseries heucherella with warm gold spring color giving way to summer lime, always with red veins that hold color well into the season. White blooms appear in June and July on short stems; the cultivar produces few or no flower spikes, reducing maintenance.

common_name: Onyx Heucherella (True Black Glossy Deeply Cut Foliage)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Onyx is a Terra Nova Nurseries heucherella introduction, among the darkest-foliaged heucherella selections, prized for foliage over bloom.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Onyx is a Terra Nova Nurseries heucherella with true black, glossy, deeply cut leaves forming a dense, medium-size mound. Shy to bloom, with flowering limited mainly to June and July.
